name: Hagia Sophia Completed, Justinian's Cathedral
summary: Emperor Justinian I dedicates the rebuilt Hagia Sophia (Church of Holy Wisdom) in Constantinople on December 27, 537, reportedly exclaiming 'Solomon, I have surpassed thee.' Built in just five years by 10,000 workers under architects Anthemius of Tralles and Isidorus of Miletus, the dome of 31 meters diameter appears to float on a ring of windows. The church serves as the center of Eastern Christianity for nearly a thousand years until the Ottoman conquest (1453).

_quarry.structural_significance: Hagia Sophia's dome represents the peak of late antique architectural achievement; its preservation through the Byzantine and Ottoman periods makes it a unique monument to the transition between Christian and Islamic civilization; its conversion to a mosque (1453) and eventual museum (1934)/mosque (2020) status makes it a permanent geopolitical symbol; the engineering innovations developed for its construction influence Byzantine and eventually Ottoman mosque architecture
